issues.description: 01_sdc_issuer.R and 01_sdc_bond.R write CSV files, while 02_sdc_processing.do opens the issuer output with Stata use and 11_gsz.do expects the bond output as DTA. This is a known CSV-to-DTA staging task; the supplied code does not perform it. Confirm the converted headers/types against the consumers and keep the agreed source root consistent.

The producer-consumer graph spans R, Stata and SAS. The supplied code uses multiple machine roots and inconsistent working directories: 03 switches from Timeliness to Documents/Temp and then reads Windows paths; 04 writes sample data to Round 2 new; 10 step1 reads sample from Analysis and inherits cwd for tempunderwriter; 11 starts in Round 3 while reading products written to Round 2 new. The root layout and order are known and can be staged coherently in a job-local relative tree.

11_gsz.do actively reads RetailTradesAltControl20190530.dta as a distinct alternative-control table. The supplied 05_retail_trades.sas exports RetailTrades20190530.dta only; no producer for the alternative-control table or its field/selection contract is supplied.

10_step3 copies fileidentifier PDFs to Dropbox Rawdata/Timeliness/Financial Statement Files, while 10_step4 counts PDFs from a separate removable-volume Financial Statement Files directory. The exact same matched PDF names can be placed under one job-local relative folder and used by both stages.

09_SingleAudit.sas comments that SingleAuditTemp.dta is created in the main do file using SingleAudit20052016, but no program among the 15 supplied entry points creates SingleAuditTemp.dta. The prepared input or an exact compatible producer/source contract is still required for this standalone branch.

evidence.description: The datasource sheet establishes the 2009–2014 target period and the SDC and MSRB input families.
evidence.quote:
The main sample period covers 2009 to 2014. The steps to clean the raw data are described
  below. Please refer to the README file, which explains the codes for each step.

  (a) SDC
      i.   Create two output files at the issuer- (6-digit CUSIP) year-issuance level and the bond-
           (9-digit CUSIP) year-issuance level. Both files include issuance-level characteristics
           (e.g., callable) included in the SDC data. If an issuance covers multiple bonds or
           issuers, the issuance characteristics will be replicated for each bond or issuer. The
           years are defined from July 1st to June 30th. For example, year 2009 refers to July 1st,
           2009 to June 30th, 2010. An issuer’s underwriter in the case of multiple underwriters
           is defined as the underwriter with the largest market share in that year.
      ii. Create a Stata file at the issuer-year level to be merged with the disclosure data.
  (b) MSRB disclosures
      i.   We assign MSRB disclosures into years, where years are defined from July 1st to June
           30th. For example, year 2009 refers to July 1st, 2009 to June 30th, 2010.
      ii. MSRB contains two types of disclosures, event based (for example, ratings downgrade)

evidence.description: The datasource sheet requires Mergent recalibration, lagged state macro data, MSRB trades, SDC ratings/underwriters, Single Audit, and a 2007–2014 bond-year yield branch.
evidence.quote:
(c) Merge SDC with MSRB Disclosure
      i.   Merge SDC and Change in scale (i.e., recalibration) from Mergent by issuer.
      ii. Merge MSRB disclosure data by issuer and year.
      iii. Merge macro variables by state and year, lagging the macro variables by one year.
      iv. Merge secondary market trading data from MSRB (trading volume and bond yield) by
          issuer and year
      v. Merge credit rating and underwriter data from SDC by issuer and year.
      vi. Merge Single Audit data based on the issuer name.
  (d) For the parallel trends analysis of the secondary market bond yield, we merge the sample
      constructed above with MSRB secondary market trading data by issuer-year. The analysis
      is performed at the bond-year level, covering 2007 to 2014. All statistics are averaged for a
      given bond-year, weighted by trade size whenever appropriate.

05_retail_trades.sas

This file processes the MSRB trading data to produce retail and institutional trading variables at the bond-year level.

06_underwriters_2.R

This file processes the SDC data to generate underwriter characteristics at the issuer-year level.   

07_bond_yield.sas

This file processes the MSRB trading data to generate volume weighted bond yield at the bond-year level. 

08_info_asym.sas

This file processes the MSRB trading data to generate Amihud price impact at the issuer-year level. 

09_SingleAudit.sas

This file processes the single audit data to merge with the main sample. 

10_page_length_step1-4.

These files process the MSRB disclosure data to compute the page length of the PDF submission files.

This file combines the main sample in step 3 with the variables produced in step 4-10 and generates the regression outputs.

* sanity check, should be zero

tsfill,full
tab year
count if cusipid == .
* 0

* Fill in data of the missing year

by cusipid: replace cusip_6 = cusip_6[_n-1] if cusip_6 ==""
foreach var of varlist mktshr leadmng leadmng1 numstate{
	by cusipid: replace `var'=`var'[_n-1] if missing(`var')
}

gsort cusipid -year

foreach var of varlist mktshr leadmng leadmng1 numstate{
	by cusipid: replace `var'=`var'[_n-1] if missing(`var')
}

* Check if all non-missing

evidence.description: The appendix describes the supplied information-asymmetry analysis and its one-year/five-year windows.
evidence.quote:
IA.7   Information asymmetry tests

       In this test, we examine changes in information asymmetry around the recalibration.

Specifically, we estimate the same specification as column (6) of Table 3, Panel B, except that we

replace our dependent variable with measures of information asymmetry, Volume and

PriceImpact. Consistent with prior literature, we do not find a significant change in these measures

around the recalibration, both in a one-year and five-year window (Cornaggia et al. [2018]). We

also fail to find a significant change in information asymmetry around the recalibration after

controlling for disclosure levels, suggesting that the insignificant change in information

asymmetry following recalibration is not driven by a decline in disclosure. These results are

inconsistent with the information content channel driving our results. We present our results in

Table IA.7. Columns (1)–(4) use a one-year window, following the recalibration (sample of 5,184

observations), and columns (5)–(8) use our full five-year window (sample of 13,300 observations).
